Replaces standard intentional injury exclusion to also exclude bodily injury resulting from conduct 'equivalent to an intentional tort, however defined, or other conduct, such that you lose your immunity from civil liability under the workers' compensation law.' Florida-specific statutory compliance endorsement mirroring FL's 'substantial certainty' intentional tort doctrine. endorsements.name: Experience Rating Modification Factor Revision Endorsement

AZ: 0.690 (credit $13,885 from base premium of $44,253). AR: 0.660. CO: 0.690. AZ also carries Schedule Modification of 0.750 (additional credit $7,726).

endorsements.name: Arizona Cancellation and Nonrenewal Endorsement
endorsements.notes: AZ-specific cancellation provisions. Insured may cancel anytime with written notice. Carrier must provide 30 days notice of cancellation or nonrenewal to insured and AZ Industrial Commission. Electronic notice permitted under AZ law.

endorsements.name: Terrorism Risk Insurance Program Reauthorization Act Disclosure Endorsement
endorsements.notes: Also referenced as 000422C0121 in schedule (pg 76). TRIA disclosure. WC covers terrorism losses as required by state law. Federal backstop applies if aggregate industry losses exceed $200M. Carrier deductible is 20% of prior year direct earned premium. Present in all states.

endorsements.name: 90-Day Reporting Requirement — Notification of Change in Ownership Endorsement
endorsements.notes: Also referenced as 000414A0119 in schedule (pg 76). Insured must report any change in ownership within 90 days. Failure may result in revision of experience rating modification factor and premium adjustment. SIGNIFICANT for PE-backed client — any ownership change, recapitalization, or acquisition must be disclosed to carrier. Present in all states.

endorsements.name: Audit Noncompliance Charge Endorsement
endorsements.notes: If insured fails to cooperate with audit, carrier may apply Audit Noncompliance Charge up to 2x estimated annual premium. Non-cooperation may result in cancellation.

endorsements.name: Arizona Amendatory Endorsement
endorsements.notes: Confirms policy period 04/01/2025 to 04/01/2026, 12:01 a.m. in insured's time zone.

endorsements.name: Part Five-Premium Amendatory Endorsement
endorsements.notes: Amends Section A (Our Manuals) to define premium manuals by reference to filed/approved rate bureau or carrier filings. Amends Section D (Premium Payments) to specify audit and retrospective premium due dates per billing.

endorsements.name: Trade or Economic Sanctions Endorsement
endorsements.notes: Also referenced as 990612 0216 in schedule (pg 77). Coverage excluded to the extent trade or economic sanctions prohibit carrier from providing insurance or paying claims. Standard exclusion across all states. Low practical impact for this client.

endorsements.name: Catastrophe (Other Than Certified Acts of Terrorism) Premium Endorsement
endorsements.notes: Also referenced as 000421F0822 in schedule (pg 77). Notification of premium charge for non-terrorism catastrophe coverage. Catastrophe defined as single event generating aggregate WC losses exceeding $50M. Present in most states.

endorsements.name: Arkansas Amendatory Endorsement
endorsements.notes: AR-specific. Amends Part Two exclusions re: punitive/exemplary damages per AR Bulletin 4-82. Amends cancellation: insured must give 30 days notice; carrier must give 10 days notice for nonpayment, 30 days for other reasons, notice to both insured and AR Workers Compensation Commission.

endorsements.name: Policy Amendatory Endorsement — California
endorsements.notes: CA-specific WC amendments: (1) Minors illegally employed not covered; (2) Punitive/exemplary damages uninsurable where prohibited by law; (3) Late indemnity payment increases subject to reimbursement by insured; (4) Amends Part One 'How This Insurance Applies' for CA disease causation standard; (5) Premium subject to CA Insurance Commissioner rate orders; (6) Long-term policy provisions; (7) Employee first lien on policy proceeds; (8) Amends final premium calculation including short-rate cancellation.

endorsements.name: Employers Liability Coverage Amendatory Endorsement — California
endorsements.notes: Amends Part Two for CA: (1) Amends 'How This Insurance Applies' for CA disease standard; (2) Modifies exclusions — deletes exclusion 2, amends exclusion 1 (contractual liability) and exclusion 7 (personnel practices); (3) Adds exclusions for: flying crew bodily injury; employee injury where employer failed to secure WC obligations; liability under CA Labor Code Section 2810.3 (labor contracting).

endorsements.name: California Cancellation Endorsement
endorsements.notes: CA-specific cancellation. Carrier may cancel for 11 specified reasons including nonpayment, audit failure, material misrepresentation, failure to cooperate with claim investigation, safety order violations, material ownership change, operations change. 10 days notice for reasons (a)–(f); 30 days for (g)–(k).

endorsements.name: Optional Premium Increase Endorsement — California
endorsements.notes: If insured fails to provide payroll audit access within 90 days after policy expiration, premium increases to 3x estimated annual premium. Additional cost recovery if access denied after third request.

endorsements.name: California Short-Rate Cancellation Endorsement and Factor Table
endorsements.notes: If insured cancels CA coverage, final premium calculated using short-rate table (higher than pro-rata). Table spans pages 150–153.

endorsements.name: Colorado Classification Endorsement
endorsements.notes: Amends Part Five (Premium) for CO. Restricts upward reclassification to situations where misclassification was caused by insured's failure to provide accurate data. Requires insured to notify carrier within 90 days of operational changes. Allows collection/refund of improper classification premiums during policy term and for 12 months after expiration.

endorsements.name: Florida Insufficient Funds Endorsement
endorsements.notes: Authorizes carrier to impose up to $15 insufficient funds fee per occurrence for returned/declined premium payments. Fee waived if failure resulted from fraud or misuse not attributable to insured.

endorsements.name: Florida Premium Due Date Endorsement
endorsements.notes: Replaces Part Five, Section D (Premium Payments) for FL. Confirms premium is due as specified in billing; premium obligation survives any invalidity of WC law.

endorsements.name: Florida Non-Cooperation With Premium Audit Endorsement
endorsements.notes: If insured fails to cooperate with final audit: (1) carrier may charge up to 3x most recent estimated annual premium after two good-faith attempts; (2) carrier has up to 3 years post-termination to reopen audit; (3) $500 inspection cost charge if physical access denied; (4) 10x penalty plus attorney's fees for understating/concealing payroll or misrepresenting classifications. Significant enforcement teeth.

endorsements.name: Florida Workers Compensation Insurance Guaranty Association Surcharge Endorsement
endorsements.notes: Requires carrier to bill and collect FL WC Guaranty Association surcharge per FL OIR order. Current surcharge rate: 0.00%. Failure to pay surcharge results in pro rata cancellation.

endorsements.name: Florida Cancellation and Nonrenewal Endorsement
endorsements.notes: Replaces Part Six-Conditions Section D for FL. 10-day notice for nonpayment; 30-day for policies in force ≤60 days; 45-day for policies in force >60 days. After 61 days, carrier may only cancel for material misstatement, nonpayment, underwriting noncompliance, substantial change in risk, or class-wide cancellation. Nonrenewal requires 45-day advance notice.

endorsements.name: Georgia Cancellation, Nonrenewal, and Change Endorsement
endorsements.notes: 10-day notice for new policies or nonpayment; 75-day certified mail notice for policies in force ≥60 days cancelled for non-payment reasons or nonrenewal. If premium increases >15% for reasons other than risk/exposure change or audit, 45-day advance notice required.

endorsements.name: Illinois Amendatory Endorsement
endorsements.notes: Modifies four sections: (1) Part Two-B expanded to include civil union partners; (2) Part Five-G Audit extended to 3 years post-policy; (3) Part Six-A Inspection clarified; (4) Part Six-D Cancellation replaced — 10-day notice for nonpayment, 30-day for policies ≤60 days, 60-day for policies >60 days. After 60 days, carrier may cancel only for enumerated reasons. Nonrenewal requires 60-day advance notice.

endorsements.name: Illinois Workers Compensation and Employers Liability Insurance Policy Exclusion Endorsement
endorsements.notes: Also referenced as 120306A0711 in schedule (pg 85). Modifies Part Two-C Exclusions Item 1. Excludes: liability assumed under a contract AND any agreement to waive the right to limit liability for contribution to WC benefits. Exception preserved for workmanlike manner warranties only. Relevant if client has IL contracts requiring broad indemnification or WC contribution waivers.

endorsements.name: Illinois Renewal Endorsement
endorsements.notes: Carrier must provide 60-day written notice of intent to renew if premium increases ≥30% or coverage materially changes. Conditional renewal notice required per 215 ILCS 5/462a if renewal premium exceeds 5% above IL DOI rate recommendation. Failure to give 60-day notice results in automatic one-year extension at current terms, with premium increase capped at 30%.

endorsements.name: Premium Due Date Endorsement
endorsements.notes: Replaces Part Five Section D. Premium must be paid when due even if part of WC law is not valid. Due date for audit and retrospective premiums is the billing date.

endorsements.name: Minnesota Cancellation and Nonrenewal Endorsement
endorsements.notes: New policies (<90 days): may cancel for any reason with 60-day advance notice. Policies ≥90 days or renewals: may cancel only for enumerated reasons. Nonpayment cancellation requires 30-day advance notice stating amount due — voids if payment made before effective date. Nonrenewal requires 60-day advance written notice. Carrier cancellation: pro rata refund. Insured cancellation: less than pro rata.

endorsements.name: Minnesota Amendatory Endorsement
endorsements.notes: Three modifications: (1) Part Two-E 'We Will Also Pay' expanded; (2) Part Two-H Recovery From Others — subrogation rights cannot be exercised against a party also insured by carrier for same loss due to nonintentional acts; (3) Part Five-G Audit for EL limited to one year post-policy (vs. three years for WC portion).

endorsements.name: Minnesota Compliance with Applicable Trade Sanction Laws
endorsements.notes: Insurance does not apply to the extent trade or economic sanctions laws prohibit carrier from providing insurance. MN-specific sanctions exclusion.

endorsements.name: New York Limit of Liability Endorsement
endorsements.notes: CRITICAL COVERAGE MODIFICATION (favorable to insured): For Part Two (Employers Liability), carrier may NOT limit its liability to pay damages for bodily injury arising out of and in the course of employment compensable under NY Workers' Compensation Law. The standard Employers Liability limits shown in Item 3.B. do NOT cap exposure for NY operations — effectively unlimited EL carrier exposure for NY-compensable injuries. Favorable to insured.

endorsements.name: New York Construction Classification Premium Adjustment Program (NYCCPAP) Explanatory Endorsement
endorsements.notes: Premium credits available for certain NY construction class codes where average wages exceed $23.24/hour. Application must be submitted to NY Compensation Insurance Rating Board at least 3 months before renewal. Administrative — no coverage impact.

endorsements.name: Catastrophe (Other Than Certified Acts of Terrorism) Premium Endorsement — New York
endorsements.notes: Separate from WC 00 04 21 F. Notification of premium charge for WC losses from Catastrophe (earthquake, noncertified terrorism, or catastrophic industrial accident) resulting in aggregate WC losses >$50M. NY-specific placement.

endorsements.name: North Carolina Amended Coverage Endorsement
endorsements.notes: Replaces Part Six-D Cancellation with Cancellation and Nonrenewal for NC. New policies (<60 days): cancel for any reason with 30-day notice. Policies ≥60 days or renewals: enumerated reasons only with 15-day written notice. Nonrenewal: 45-day advance notice required. Premium increase for reasons within carrier's exclusive control: 30-day advance written notice required.

endorsements.name: Oregon Cancellation Endorsement
endorsements.notes: Replaces Part Six-D Cancellation for OR. Carrier cancellation notice periods: 90 days if exiting the insured's entire premium category; 45 days for other reasons; 10 days for nonpayment.

endorsements.name: Oregon Amendatory Endorsement
endorsements.notes: Modifies Part Two-C (Exclusions) Item 5 — replaces intentional injury exclusion with OR-specific language per ORS 656.156 and ORS 656.018(3). Adds new Exclusion 13 to Part Two-C: excludes any cause of action or remedy arising out of ORS 656.019 or ORS 654.305–654.336 (OR OSHA civil liability provisions).

endorsements.name: Oregon Limits of Liability Endorsement
endorsements.notes: Also referenced as 360306 0102 in schedule (pg 91). Sets minimum Employers Liability limits for OR operations: $500,000 each accident / $500,000 policy limit / $500,000 each employee (bodily injury by disease), or the amount shown in Item 3.B., whichever is greater. Applies to OR operations only.

endorsements.name: Oregon Confidentiality Endorsement
endorsements.notes: Restricts employer use of confidential medical and vocational claim information provided by insurer. Employer must hold in confidence, restrict disclosure, and not use to discriminate against injured workers.

endorsements.name: Oregon Employer Paid Medical Claims Endorsement
endorsements.notes: Allows employer to voluntarily reimburse carrier for medical payments on accepted nondisabling claims up to a defined maximum. Reimbursed amounts excluded from experience rating calculations.

endorsements.name: Notice of Election to Accept or Reject Insurance Deductible — Illinois
endorsements.notes: Insured elected NO deductible (signed 04/01/2025). Illinois deductible option declined.

endorsements.name: Illinois Industrial Commission Operations Fund Surcharge Disclosure
endorsements.notes: Policyholder disclosure regarding 1.092% surcharge on IL WC premium. Surcharge amount: $2.00.

endorsements.name: Pennsylvania Employer Assessment Endorsement
endorsements.notes: PA Act 57 of 1997 assessment endorsement. Code 0938, Employer Assessment Factor applied, Assessment $6.00.

endorsements.name: Pennsylvania Merit Rating Plan Endorsement
endorsements.notes: 5% premium credit (Stat Code 9885) for zero lost-time injuries; no adjustment for one lost-time injury (Stat Code 9884); 5% surcharge (Stat Code 9886) for two or more lost-time injuries. Applies to risks below the Experience Rating Plan threshold.

endorsements.name: Pennsylvania Audit Noncompliance Charge Endorsement
endorsements.notes: Allows carrier to apply Audit Noncompliance Charge equal to 2x estimated annual premium if insured refuses audit. ANC removed if insured later cooperates. Carrier must make two documented attempts before applying ANC.

endorsements.name: Pennsylvania Notice — Insurance Consultation Services Exemption Act
endorsements.notes: Carrier not liable for damages arising from loss control surveys or inspections per Pennsylvania's ICSE Act. Exceptions for negligence during actual performance or gross negligence/malice. Informational.

endorsements.name: Pennsylvania Act 86-1986 Endorsement — Nonrenewal and Notice of Premium Increase
endorsements.notes: Requires 60-day advance notice of nonrenewal, 30-day advance notice of premium increase. On carrier cancellation, unearned premium returned within 10 business days; insured cancellation within 30 days. Final audit adjustment within 15 days of computation.

endorsements.name: Special Pennsylvania Endorsement — Inspection of Manuals
endorsements.notes: Notice that manuals of rules, rating plans, and classifications are filed with the Pennsylvania Insurance Commissioner. Administrative/regulatory compliance.

endorsements.name: South Dakota Direct Action Statute Endorsement
endorsements.notes: Allows injured employee (or survivors) to add the insurer as a direct defendant in a damages suit against the employer under Part Two (Employers Liability). Carrier is directly liable to pay damages for which the employer is liable.

endorsements.name: South Dakota Cancellation and Nonrenewal Endorsement
endorsements.notes: Insured may cancel anytime with written notice. Carrier must file notice with SD Dept. of Labor: 10 days for nonpayment, 20 days for other reasons. After 60 days from inception, cancellation limited to enumerated reasons. Nonrenewal requires 60-day advance notice to insured and agent.

endorsements.name: Pending Rate Change Endorsement — Multi-State
endorsements.notes: Same form applied to 12 states. Notifies insured that rate change filings are pending regulatory approval in each listed state. If approved, new endorsements will be issued showing revised rates. Administrative — no immediate coverage impact.

endorsements.name: Child Labor Laws and Contractors Responsibility
endorsements.notes: Present in most states. Addresses contractor responsibility for compliance with child labor laws. Administrative.

exclusions_of_note.name: Employment Practices — Employers' Liability Exclusion
exclusions_of_note.impact: Part Two, Section C, Exclusion 7: EL coverage does not apply to 'damages arising out of coercion, criticism, demotion, evaluation, reassignment, discipline, defamation, harassment, humiliation, discrimination against or termination of any employee, or any personnel practices, policies, acts or omissions.' Standard — EPLI is a separate policy — but confirms WC/EL policy does not backstop any employment claims.

exclusions_of_note.name: Contractual Liability Exclusion — Employers' Liability
exclusions_of_note.impact: Part Two, Section C, Exclusion 1: EL does not cover 'liability assumed under a contract,' except for a warranty that work will be done in a workmanlike manner. If a contract requires the insured to indemnify a third party for employee injury claims, that contractual assumption of liability is NOT covered under Part Two. Workers' Comp Part One still pays statutory benefits regardless.

exclusions_of_note.name: Federal Acts Exclusions — Employers' Liability
exclusions_of_note.impact: Part Two, Section C, Exclusions 8–10: EL excludes claims subject to USL&H Act, Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentalities Act, Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act, Defense Base Act, Federal Mine Safety and Health Act, FELA, and maritime/crew member claims. No USL&H or maritime exposure apparent for Runbeck, but noted for completeness.

exclusions_of_note.name: Intentional Acts — Florida Modified Exclusion
exclusions_of_note.impact: Florida-specific modification broadens the intentional acts exclusion to encompass conduct amounting to an intentional tort under FL law, including where the employer loses WC immunity. This is a Florida statutory compliance endorsement — it mirrors FL law, not an additional coverage gap.

exclusions_of_note.name: Illinois Contractual Liability and Contribution Waiver Exclusion
exclusions_of_note.impact: Under IL law, excludes coverage for liability assumed under any contract AND any agreement to waive the right to limit liability for contribution to WC benefits. Exception preserved for workmanlike manner warranties. Relevant if client has IL contracts requiring broad indemnification or WC contribution waivers — those contractual obligations are not backed by this policy for IL operations.

exclusions_of_note.name: Indiana Other States Insurance and Voluntary Compensation Exclusion
exclusions_of_note.impact: Excludes Other States Insurance and Voluntary Compensation for Indiana, reverting Indiana to the base NCCI form. Limits flexibility if Indiana employees travel or temporarily work in unlisted states without prior policy endorsement.

exclusions_of_note.name: Trade or Economic Sanctions Exclusion
exclusions_of_note.impact: No coverage where providing insurance or paying claims is prohibited by trade or economic sanctions. Standard endorsement across all states. Low practical impact for a domestic election services company. MN has a parallel state-specific provision under WC 22 03 01 (pg 178).

exclusions_of_note.name: California — Minors Illegally Employed
exclusions_of_note.impact: No coverage for additional compensation under CA Labor Code Section 4557 for injury to employees under 16 illegally employed. Standard CA exclusion; not relevant unless client employs minors in CA.

exclusions_of_note.name: California — Punitive and Exemplary Damages
exclusions_of_note.impact: No coverage for punitive or exemplary damages where insurance of such liability is prohibited by law. Standard CA statutory exclusion.

exclusions_of_note.name: California Employers Liability — Labor Contracting (CA Labor Code Section 2810.3)
exclusions_of_note.impact: Employers Liability coverage excludes liability arising from CA Labor Code Section 2810.3 (labor contractor client liability). If client uses labor contractors or staffing firms for CA operations, this exclusion could create an uninsured gap for joint employer liability under CA's labor contractor law.

exclusions_of_note.name: California Employers Liability — Failure to Secure WC Obligations
exclusions_of_note.impact: No EL coverage where employer is deprived of statutory defenses due to failure to comply with CA WC law. Standard CA exclusion — penalty for non-compliance falls on employer.

exclusions_of_note.name: Oregon Intentional Tort and OSHA Civil Liability Exclusion
exclusions_of_note.impact: Oregon-specific exclusion for: (1) bodily injury intentionally caused or aggravated by employer, or resulting from conduct equivalent to an intentional tort per ORS 656.156 or ORS 656.018(3), causing employer to lose WC immunity; AND (2) any cause of action under ORS 656.019 or ORS 654.305–654.336 (OR OSHA civil liability provisions). If an Oregon employee successfully argues employer's intentional conduct voided WC immunity, EL coverage under Part Two will not respond. State-mandated.
